text:
Artemi Panarin turned 35 last week and is still the engine of the Kings' attack. He has 17 points in 14 games, and Los Angeles takes 59% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, almost 17 points better than without him. That gap is the loudest thing in his profile.

His luck runs both ways, which is why our numbers trust the points. His own shooting is hot: 8 goals on 5.1 expected, 18% after 12% last season. But his teammates have finished 4.9 goals below their chances with him out there, which has cost him assists. One should cool as the other warms.

The Kings have been all or nothing lately, and so has he: over his last ten games he has a point in every win and none in the losses. The best of it was four assists in a 7-2 win over San Jose on Wednesday, a night The Hockey News noted he and Adrian Kempe combined for eight points. Never drafted, a Calder winner after three KHL seasons, and our projection still has him near 94 points. Watch that five-on-five share; at 35, it's what will tell you first if he's slowing.
headline: Panarin at 35: luck in both directions
